q: Does UCCSD-VQE still reach chemical accuracy vs FCI for the paper's strongly-correlated open-shell cases (:CH2, CH2 singlet-triplet gap, N2 near-dissociation), or does the CCSD = UCCSD-VQE analytical identity fail empirically where CCSD itself is known to be a poor reference?
basis: Paper reports UCCSD-VQE ≈ CCSD for H2 and LiH (closed-shell); this replication verified only those two. For open-shell CH2 and stretched N2, single-reference CCSD is documented in the literature to break down, so the identity UCCSD-VQE = CCSD would inherit that breakdown and the paper's headline 'chemical accuracy for all 9 molecules' claim needs an empirical check where FCI is still tractable.
next_steps: On the same qiskit-nature + PySCF stack, run classical UCCSD (as proxy for converged UCCSD-VQE) and full FCI for (a) :CH2 STO-3G singlet ground state, (b) CH2 triplet, (c) N2 STO-3G at r = 1.1, 1.5, 2.0 Å; tabulate |E_UCCSD − E_FCI| in kJ/mol and compare against the paper's <1 kJ/mol claim. Free endpoint (local CPU). Flag any case that exceeds 4 kJ/mol (≈1 kcal/mol chemical accuracy threshold).

q: How much do modern low-rank / tensor-hypercontraction (THC) integral factorizations change the paper's 2018-era CNOT-count resource estimate for the same molecules?
basis: Paper counts CNOTs for JW-mapped UCCSD Trotter with MP2 pre-screening and gate cancellation. Post-2020 work (von Burg et al. 2021; Lee, Berry et al. 2021 THC for QPE; DF/CDF for VQE by Motta et al. 2021) has repeatedly shown 10–100× reductions in T-count / CNOT-count from integral factorization alone. Paper's resource extrapolation to 10^5–10^7 CNOTs was pre-THC; whether their conclusion 'UCCSD-VQE is beyond near-term hardware for interesting molecules' still holds with modern factorization is an open question this replication does not answer.
next_steps: Reimplement the paper's LiH and H2O STO-3G Hamiltonian in OpenFermion / PennyLane with DF or CDF factorization; compare transpiled CNOT counts to paper's Table SI I. If reductions of ≥3× hold, note that the paper's near-term-feasibility conclusion may need revision. Free endpoint (OpenFermion + PennyLane on CPU).

q: Does UCCSD-VQE combined with an active-space reduction (CASSCF-selected orbitals + UCCSD over the active space) achieve the paper's chemical-accuracy target with dramatically fewer qubits than the paper's full-orbital JW mapping suggests?
basis: Paper uses full orbital → full JW mapping (6 spatial → 12 qubits for LiH STO-3G). Modern practice in NISQ chemistry papers (Grimsley et al. 2019 ADAPT-VQE, Ryabinkin et al. 2018 iQCC) uses active-space partitioning to fit real molecules in <10 qubits without losing chemical accuracy for the property of interest. Paper does not discuss this trade-off; its resource-vs-accuracy Pareto frontier may be pessimistic by an order of magnitude in qubit count for practical use.
next_steps: Run CAS(4,4) + UCCSD-VQE for LiH and H2O STO-3G on qiskit-nature; compare qubit count and E_corr recovery vs the full-space numbers from this replication + paper's Table SI I. Report the qubit-count vs |E − E_FCI| Pareto curve. Free endpoint (local CPU).

q: How does UCCSD-VQE at its converged energy compare against modern classical baselines (DMRG with M=1000 bond dimension, CCSD(T), CCSDT) for the same molecule set, and does the paper's implicit case for 'why bother with a quantum computer' survive that comparison?
basis: Paper's main scientific pitch is that VQE gives FCI-quality answers. But for the 9 small molecules in Table SI I, classical DMRG with modest bond dimension is known to reach FCI to sub-mHa on all of them at commodity-CPU cost, and CCSD(T) reaches chemical accuracy for closed-shell cases. Paper does not benchmark against these classical near-exact methods, so the quantum-advantage argument is left implicit and unquantified.
next_steps: Using pyscf + block2 or CheMPS2 (free, open source), run DMRG(M=500,1000,2000) for LiH, H2O, N2 STO-3G; compare wall-clock and |E − E_FCI| against this replication's UCCSD-VQE numbers. If DMRG matches FCI to <0.1 mHa in <1 s on a laptop, that reframes the paper's resource-estimate story (quantum resources should be judged not against FCI but against DMRG). Free endpoint (CPU).

q: Under a fixed measurement budget (total shots), does measurement-optimized UCCSD-VQE (grouped Pauli measurements, classical shadows) actually beat QPE with the paper's FT-overhead assumptions for reaching chemical accuracy on LiH — i.e., is the paper's VQE-focused resource picture the right one, or should it be QPE?
basis: Paper focuses on gate-count resources for UCCSD-VQE circuits without treating the sampling cost of VQE energy evaluation, which is the actual near-term bottleneck (10^6–10^9 shots per energy for chemical accuracy). Fully-fault-tolerant QPE has poly-log shot cost but higher per-run gate cost. Paper's near-term-feasibility conclusion depends on which side of that trade-off wins, and it does not explicitly compare.
next_steps: For LiH STO-3G, estimate (a) UCCSD-VQE shots needed for E to 1 mHa via grouped-Pauli measurement (openfermion has utilities), (b) QPE ancilla + T-count for the same target using standard trotterized-block-encoding recipes (Berry et al. 2019); report the crossover total-run-time as a function of physical-gate error rate. Free endpoint (OpenFermion + local calculations). Flag which end of the trade-off the paper's implicit assumption sits on.
